intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee. Join a local-led walking tour or explore independently, hopping between street stalls and tiny plastic-stool restaurants packed with locals.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival
experiences.description: Experience the magical monthly lantern festival in Hoi An's UNESCO-listed Ancient Town. Rent a traditional ao dai outfit, release a flower lantern on the Thu Bon River, and explore centuries-old merchant houses, tailor shops, and temples illuminated by hundreds of colorful silk lanterns.

experiences.name: Motorbike Loop Through Ha Giang
experiences.description: Rent a semi-automatic motorbike and tackle the legendary Ha Giang Loop, a 350km backpacker circuit through dramatic karst mountains, terraced rice fields, and remote ethnic minority villages. Interact with Hmong and Dao communities and stay in budget guesthouses along the route.

experiences.name: Banh Mi and Cao Lau Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Hoi An where a local chef teaches you to make regional specialties like Cao Lau noodles, White Rose dumplings, and crispy Banh Mi. Visit the local market to source fresh ingredients before cooking and enjoying your meal together.

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Sampan Boat Tour
experiences.description: Hop on a traditional wooden sampan boat to navigate the narrow canals of the Mekong Delta. Visit floating markets, coconut candy workshops, and rice paper factories. Sample tropical fruits, fresh spring rolls, and elephant ear fish while experiencing the authentic rural lifestyle of southern Vietnam.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 - No morning activities scheduled. Rest on the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the airport, clear customs and immigration. Take a budget shuttle bus or shared taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a slow walk along the beachfront to get your bearings. Explore the immediate surroundings of the resort and nearby streets.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearest local night market or street food strip within walking distance of the resort. Explore stalls, sample snacks, and soak in the Vietnamese coastal atmosphere. Pick up a local SIM card at a convenience store for cheap data.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick Bánh mì sandwich from a street vendor near the airport or bus station (~15,000–25,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Local street food market near the resort — try Bún bò Huế or Phở from a roadside stall (~40,000–60,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some cash to Vietnamese Dong (VND) at the airport for better rates. Avoid metered taxis without verified meters — use Grab app for safe, cheap rides. Keep luggage light and secure.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and head to the beach at sunrise for a free and stunning experience. Walk along the shoreline, watch local fishermen bring in their morning catch. Find a local café nearby for a traditional Vietnamese breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (~80,000–150,000 VND/day) and explore the local town. Visit a nearby Buddhist temple or pagoda for a free cultural experience. Browse local markets and interact with vendors to practice bargaining.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free walking tour or self-guided street food tour of the local neighborhood. Try multiple small dishes from different vendors to maximize variety on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Bánh mì ốp la (baguette with fried egg) from a street cart (~20,000–30,000 VND) with Vietnamese iced coffee (cà phê sữa đá, ~20,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Cơm tấm (broken rice with grilled pork) from a local rice shop (~40,000–55,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food crawl — Gỏi cuốn (fresh spring rolls), grilled corn, and sugarcane juice (~60,000–80,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sunscreen and a hat — April can be hot and humid in Vietnam. Carry a reusable water bottle and refill at your hostel to save money and reduce plastic waste.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local fish market at dawn (around 5:30–7:00 AM) to see the vibrant trading culture. Photograph colorful boats and interact with fishermen. This is completely free and deeply authentic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget day trip by local bus or shared van to a nearby historical or cultural site such as a Cham temple ruin, ancient town, or rice paddy village depending on the region. Entrance fees are typically 20,000–50,000 VND.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local family-run restaurant (quán ăn). These spots serve the most authentic and affordable food in Vietnam.

meals.breakfast: Xôi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street vendor near the fish market (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Mì Quảng (turmeric noodles with pork and shrimp) at a roadside restaurant during the day trip (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Family-run quán ăn dinner — order a set rice meal with soup, vegetables, and protein (~60,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a light rain jacket as April can have occasional afternoon showers. Respect dress codes at religious sites — cover shoulders and knees.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning cooking class or visit a local herb and spice market. Many budget cooking classes run for 2–3 hours and include a market tour for around 200,000–350,000 VND. Learn to make Phở or Bánh xèo (sizzling pancake).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local museum or cultural center (entrance typically 20,000–40,000 VND). Learn about Vietnam's history, the war era, or regional ethnic minority cultures depending on your location.
day_by_day.evening: Find a rooftop bar or beachside spot for sunset watching — many places offer happy hour deals. Afterward, head to a night market for cheap street eats and souvenir browsing.

meals.breakfast: Phở bò (beef noodle soup) at a traditional phở shop (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Included in cooking class or grab Bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls) from a market stall (~25,000–40,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Night market street food — Bánh tráng nướng (grilled rice paper pizza), skewers, and fresh fruit (~70,000–90,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book cooking classes in advance through hostel noticeboards or TripAdvisor for the best budget deals. Avoid tourist-trap restaurants near major landmarks.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning — swim, snorkel, or simply relax. Many beaches in Vietnam are free. Rent snorkeling gear from local shops (~50,000–80,000 VND/hour) if available near the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget boat tour or kayaking excursion to nearby islands or sea caves. Group tours are significantly cheaper (~150,000–300,000 VND) versus private tours. Book through your hostel or local agents.
day_by_day.evening: Beachside barbecue evening — many coastal areas have vendors grilling fresh seafood right on the beach. Pick your catch and have it grilled on the spot.

meals.breakfast: Hủ tiếu (clear noodle soup) from a local stall (~35,000–50,000 VND) with fresh coconut water (~20,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from a convenience store for the boat trip — instant noodles, crackers, and fruit (~30,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Beachside BBQ — grilled squid, clams, and corn on the cob (~100,000–150,000 VND for a satisfying spread)

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate boat tour prices — always compare at least 3 vendors before booking. Apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect Vietnam's coral ecosystems.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus or train to a nearby city or town for a change of scenery. Vietnam's sleeper buses and trains are extremely affordable (~100,000–200,000 VND for short routes). Check into a budget guesthouse or hostel dorm (~100,000–180,000 VND/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the new destination's old quarter or historic district on foot. Visit a local pagoda, colonial-era architecture, or artisan workshops. Join a free walking tour if available.
day_by_day.evening: Discover the new city's food scene. Vietnam's regional cuisine varies dramatically — try dishes specific to this area that you haven't eaten yet.

meals.breakfast: Quick Bánh mì from a street cart before catching the bus (~20,000–25,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Cháo (Vietnamese rice porridge) with toppings at a local lunch spot in the new city (~30,000–45,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Regional specialty dish at a busy local restaurant — busy spots mean fresh food and local approval (~50,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book transport tickets the evening before using Baolau or 12Go Asia for the best prices. Keep a digital and physical copy of your accommodation address in Vietnamese script for taxi drivers.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a famous local landmark, heritage site, or natural attraction in your new city. Many UNESCO-listed sites in Vietnam have affordable entry fees (~50,000–150,000 VND). Arrive early to beat crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through a local market — not a tourist market, but a wet market where locals shop. Buy tropical fruits, snacks, and experience the sensory overload of Vietnamese market culture. Practice your bargaining skills.
day_by_day.evening: Find a rooftop café or street-side plastic stool bar. Order Bia hơi (fresh draught beer, ~10,000–15,000 VND per glass) and watch the city come alive at night. This is quintessential Vietnamese backpacker culture.

meals.breakfast: Bánh ướt (wet rice paper with herbs and pork) from a morning market stall (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Self-assembled lunch from the market — fresh fruit, bánh tráng, and local snacks (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bún chả (grilled pork with vermicelli) at a street restaurant (~45,000–65,000 VND) — a Vietnamese classic

day_by_day.notes: Stay hydrated — carry water everywhere. Tap water is not safe to drink; buy large 5L bottles from convenience stores (~15,000–20,000 VND) rather than small bottles for better value.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike or nature walk in a nearby national park, rice terrace area, or viewpoint. Many natural sites have free or very low-cost access. Hire a local guide for ~100,000–200,000 VND for deeper cultural insight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local artisan village or craft workshop — lacquerware, silk weaving, pottery, or lantern making depending on the region. Many workshops offer free entry and a chance to try making crafts yourself.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural performance — water puppet theater (~80,000–100,000 VND), traditional music, or a local festival if one is happening. Check hostel noticeboards for events.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the trailhead or market before the hike — Xôi chiên (fried sticky rice cake) (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Village lunch at a local home-style restaurant near the artisan village (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Pre-theater street food — Nem nướng (grilled pork rolls) and fresh spring rolls (~60,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Wear closed-toe shoes for hiking and nature walks. Mosquito repellent is essential for jungle or rural areas. Bring cash as rural areas rarely accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Return journey back toward the resort area or continue to another destination. Take a scenic local bus route rather than an express option to see more of the countryside and save money.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at a roadside attraction, viewpoint, or small town along the way. Vietnam's countryside between cities is stunning — don't rush through it. Grab snacks from roadside vendors selling local specialties.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at or near Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a final beach sunset. Reflect on the trip and do some light souvenir shopping at local shops (avoid tourist traps near resorts).

meals.breakfast: Last breakfast in the secondary city — Phở or noodle soup at a local shop (~40,000–55,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Roadside stop lunch — Cơm bình dân (budget rice plate) at a highway rest stop (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner near the resort — visit a local seafood restaurant away from the resort strip for better prices (~100,000–150,000 VND for a full meal)

day_by_day.notes: Budget tip: buy souvenirs at local markets rather than resort gift shops — prices can be 3–5x cheaper. Lacquerware, silk scarves, and coffee make excellent lightweight gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk or swim. Pack your bags and do a final check of the room. Have a leisurely last Vietnamese breakfast at a local café. Write down your favorite food spots and experiences to share with other travelers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort (standard checkout is 12:00 — ask for late checkout if your flight is evening). Store luggage at the reception. Take a final motorbike or bicycle ride through the local area. Visit any spots you missed.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport with plenty of time. Take a Grab or shared shuttle to keep costs low. Enjoy one last Bánh mì or Vietnamese iced coffee at the airport before departure.

meals.breakfast: Splurge slightly on your last morning — full Vietnamese breakfast spread at a local café: Phở, Bánh mì, and cà phê sữa đá (~80,000–100,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the resort or from a convenience store to avoid overspending on the last day (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Airport food or a final street food snack before security — Bánh mì or fresh fruit (~30,000–50,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Keep 200,000–300,000 VND in cash for airport transport and last-minute expenses. Spend remaining VND on snacks, coffee, or small gifts as it's difficult to exchange back. Take a final photo of your favorite Vietnamese meal — you'll miss it when you're gone!

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands; clear customs and collect luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (Beachfront). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get oriented with the surroundings. Explore the nearby coastal promenade and watch local fishermen at work.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearest local night market or beachside strip for a gentle first evening. Browse street food stalls, try Vietnamese iced tea (trà đá), and soak in the atmosphere without overexerting after a long flight.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bowl of phở or bánh mì from a street stall near the airport or resort area upon arrival (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Beachside local restaurant — try grilled fresh seafood (tôm nướng, mực nướng) with steamed rice (~150,000–250,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Exchange currency at the airport or a reputable exchange bureau near the resort. Purchase a local SIM card (Viettel or Mobifone) for affordable data (~100,000–150,000 VND). April weather in Vietnam is warm and humid — stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning walk along the beach at sunrise — a quintessential Vietnamese coastal experience. Watch locals perform their morning exercises and fishing boats return with the day's catch. Visit a nearby local market (chợ) to observe daily life and sample fresh tropical fruits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the cultural heart of the nearest town. Visit a local pagoda or temple, wander through the old quarter streets, and browse handicraft shops. Hire a bicycle or use a ride-hailing app (Grab) to get around affordably.
day_by_day.evening: Join a street food walking tour or self-guide through the evening food scene. Look for bún bò Huế, bánh xèo (sizzling pancakes), or local regional specialties depending on your location.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or nearby café — cà phê trứng (egg coffee) or Vietnamese drip coffee with bánh mì (~40,000–70,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Local com binh dan (everyday rice restaurant) — rice with 2–3 side dishes (~60,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food crawl — mix of small dishes from different stalls (~100,000–180,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting temples (cover shoulders and knees). Bargain respectfully at markets — start at 50–60% of the asking price. Grab app is reliable and affordable for transport.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby cultural or historical landmark — a UNESCO heritage site, ancient citadel, or traditional village depending on your region. Hire a local guide for deeper cultural context (~200,000–300,000 VND for a half-day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the historical site or visit a nearby craft village (pottery, silk weaving, or lantern making). Participate in a short hands-on workshop if available (~100,000–200,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a mid-range restaurant with a view. Try a regional specialty dish you haven't had yet.

meals.breakfast: Bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls) with pork and herbs from a local morning stall (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Restaurant near the heritage site — cao lầu or mì Quảng (regional noodles) (~80,000–120,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant with river or sea view — set menu or à la carte (~200,000–350,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book a reputable local guide through your hotel or a licensed tour operator. Carry cash as many heritage sites and small vendors don't accept cards. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Cooking class experience — join a half-day Vietnamese cooking class where you visit a local market to pick ingredients, then learn to prepare 3–4 traditional dishes (~400,000–600,000 VND per person). A fantastic way to connect culture and food.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free time at the beach or resort pool. Alternatively, explore a nearby nature spot — a lagoon, sand dunes, or mangrove forest depending on your location. Rent a kayak or paddleboard if available.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Vietnamese cultural performance (water puppetry, tuồng opera, or folk music) if available locally (~100,000–200,000 VND). Follow with dinner at a highly-rated local eatery.

meals.breakfast: Xôi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street vendor (~30,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Included in cooking class — you eat what you cook!
meals.dinner: Recommended local restaurant — lẩu (hot pot) for a communal dining experience (~200,000–300,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least one day in advance through your hotel concierge or platforms like Airbnb Experiences or GetYourGuide. Hot pot is best enjoyed with a group — great for meeting fellow travelers at the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Motorbike or bicycle exploration of the rural countryside surrounding your resort area. Ride through rice paddies, small villages, and local farms. Rent a semi-automatic motorbike (~150,000–200,000 VND/day) or bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local fishing village or riverside community. Interact with locals, observe traditional boat-building or net-weaving, and learn about their way of life. Take a short boat ride on a traditional wooden vessel (~100,000–150,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beachfront bar or rooftop spot. Enjoy the golden hour over the water, then transition to dinner at a nearby seafood restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Phở bò (beef noodle soup) at a local breakfast spot (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Roadside village eatery — simple rice and grilled fish (~60,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Seafood restaurant — whole grilled fish (cá nướng), clams (nghêu hấp sả), and morning glory stir-fry (~200,000–300,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Always wear a helmet when riding a motorbike — it's the law and essential for safety. Carry an international driving permit if you plan to ride. Fuel up the motorbike before returning. April can bring occasional afternoon showers — carry a light rain poncho (~20,000 VND at any convenience store).

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — take a scenic bus, train, or short domestic flight to a new destination within Vietnam (e.g., from central to northern or southern regions). Enjoy the journey as part of the experience — Vietnam's landscapes are stunning from train windows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the new destination. Check into a mid-range guesthouse or hostel (~300,000–600,000 VND/night). Take a gentle orientation walk around the new neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the new city's evening scene — find the local backpacker street or food alley. Try the region's signature dish and meet fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Bánh mì from a street cart near the resort before departure (~25,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Train or bus station food, or a stop at a roadside restaurant (~60,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Backpacker-friendly local restaurant in the new city — bún chả, gỏi cuốn, or regional specialty (~100,000–180,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book train or bus tickets at least 2–3 days in advance, especially for popular routes (e.g., Da Nang to Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City). The Reunification Express train offers scenic coastal views. Sleeper buses are budget-friendly for overnight routes (~200,000–350,000 VND).

day_by_day.morning: Full cultural immersion day in the new city. Visit the top historical or cultural landmark — ancient temples, a war museum, imperial citadel, or old town depending on location. Hire a local guide for 2–3 hours (~200,000–400,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore local markets and artisan districts. Visit a traditional Vietnamese coffee shop and spend time people-watching. Browse local bookshops, art galleries, or vintage shops.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a street food festival or evening market if available. Otherwise, self-guide through the city's best street food spots using a food map or local recommendations.

meals.breakfast: Cháo (rice porridge) with century egg and pork at a local breakfast stall (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bún bò Huế or regional noodle specialty at a hole-in-the-wall restaurant (~60,000–90,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food feast — multiple small dishes from different vendors: nem rán, chả giò, bánh tráng nướng (~120,000–200,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Download the Foody or Yelp Vietnam app for crowd-sourced restaurant recommendations. Many of the best street food spots have no English menus — point at what others are eating or use Google Translate's camera function.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a natural wonder — a national park, cave system, waterfall, or bay depending on your location (e.g., Phong Nha Caves, Ha Long Bay, Mekong Delta, or Sapa terraces). Book a small group tour for the best value (~400,000–800,000 VND per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the day trip — hiking, boat rides, or trekking through the natural landscape. Swim in a natural pool or bay if conditions allow.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city. Rest and recover with a traditional Vietnamese massage (~200,000–300,000 VND for 60 minutes) before a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early start — grab bánh mì or sticky rice from a street vendor before the tour pickup (~30,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Included in tour package or local restaurant near the natural site (~80,000–150,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner at a well-reviewed local restaurant — try thịt kho tàu (caramelized pork and eggs) with jasmine rice (~150,000–250,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Bring sunscreen, insect repellent, a hat, and plenty of water for outdoor activities. April can be hot and humid — pace yourself during hikes. Confirm tour pickup times and inclusions when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning for independent exploration — revisit a favorite spot, do some souvenir shopping, or simply enjoy a slow Vietnamese breakfast and coffee. Visit a local café culture spot and journal your trip highlights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a street photography walk through the most photogenic neighborhoods — French colonial architecture, colorful alleyways, or flower markets. Visit a local art gallery or cultural center.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer farewell dinner at a well-regarded mid-range restaurant. Try a multi-course Vietnamese tasting menu or a regional specialty you haven't yet experienced.

meals.breakfast: Slow breakfast at a charming Vietnamese café — cà phê sữa đá (iced milk coffee) with bánh mì or croissant (~60,000–90,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bún thịt nướng (grilled pork vermicelli bowl) at a local favorite (~70,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant with curated Vietnamese menu — chả cá Lã Vọng, pho bo, or com tấm sườn (~250,000–400,000 VND per person including drinks)

day_by_day.notes: Good souvenir buys: lacquerware, silk scarves, hand-embroidered items, Vietnamese coffee and filters, artisan ceramics, and local tea. Negotiate at markets but pay fair prices — remember the economic context. Keep receipts for customs if buying valuable items.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise moment (beach, rooftop, or viewpoint). Pack and complete checkout. Take a final walk through your favorite local street or market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to the airport or bus/train station for onward journey. Allow extra time for traffic and check-in procedures. If time permits, grab one last bowl of phở or Vietnamese iced coffee before departing.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or travel to next destination. Reflect on 10 incredible days of Vietnamese culture, food, and adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final Vietnamese breakfast — phở or bún bò at a beloved local spot (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or last street food stop near the terminal (~80,000–150,000 VND)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at next destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2–3 hours before international flights, 90 minutes for domestic. Spend remaining Vietnamese Dong on snacks, coffee, or small gifts at the airport. Keep some cash for any last-minute transport or tips. Vietnam requires no departure tax for most nationalities — confirm visa requirements for your return or onward journey.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — No morning activities scheduled. Rest and freshen up after the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome drink and resort orientation. Take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to acclimate and soak in the surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar, followed by a relaxed exploration of the nearest local night market to get a first taste of Vietnamese street food culture.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the resort's signature restaurant upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium beachfront seafood restaurant near the resort, featuring fresh catches grilled to order with local spices and herbs

day_by_day.notes: Allow time to rest and recover from jet lag. Keep Day 1 light and relaxing. Confirm all upcoming tours and private transfers with the resort concierge upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided cultural walking tour of the nearest historic old town or heritage quarter. Visit ancient temples, colonial architecture, and local artisan workshops. Enjoy a traditional Vietnamese iced coffee at a renowned local café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive street food tour by private cyclo (pedicab) through local markets and food stalls. Sample bánh mì, phở, gỏi cuốn (fresh spring rolls), and regional specialties with a private culinary guide.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Vietnamese water puppet show or live cultural performance at a nearby arts center, followed by a fine dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Lavish breakfast buffet at the resort featuring both Vietnamese and international options including congee, fresh tropical fruits, and Vietnamese egg coffee
meals.lunch: Street food tasting lunch curated by a private food guide — multiple stops including a heritage pho house and a bánh mì institution
meals.dinner: Dinner at an award-winning Vietnamese fine dining restaurant featuring elevated regional cuisine with wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. Bring cash in Vietnamese Dong for street food stalls. The cyclo street food tour should be booked in advance through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise boat excursion to a nearby bay or coastal area. Enjoy the tranquil scenery, spot local fishing villages, and snorkel in crystal-clear waters with premium snorkeling gear provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a UNESCO-listed heritage site or nearby island. Explore ancient ruins, pagodas, or traditional fishing villages with a private historian guide. Photography opportunities abound.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a luxury spa treatment — choose from a traditional Vietnamese herbal wrap, hot stone massage, or aromatherapy session at the resort spa.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast box prepared by the resort for the sunrise boat excursion — Vietnamese sticky rice parcels, fresh fruit, and thermos of Vietnamese coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on the boat or at a floating restaurant in the bay — grilled prawns, steamed clams, and local fish with dipping sauces
meals.dinner: In-resort private dining experience on the beach — a curated tasting menu with Vietnamese fusion dishes served under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Bring sunscreen, a hat, and reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling. The private beach dinner should be reserved 24 hours in advance with the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class with a celebrated local chef. Learn to prepare 4–5 traditional Vietnamese dishes including pho broth from scratch, fresh spring rolls, and a regional specialty dessert. Class held in an authentic local kitchen or heritage home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wet market with the chef to source fresh ingredients, then explore nearby artisan craft shops selling lacquerware, silk, and handmade ceramics. Perfect for premium souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset rooftop cocktail experience at a luxury sky bar in the nearest city center, followed by dinner.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — Vietnamese-style savory crepes (bánh xèo) and fresh coconut smoothies
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class in an intimate setting with your chef host
meals.dinner: Dinner at a rooftop fine dining restaurant with panoramic city or ocean views — contemporary Vietnamese cuisine with premium cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Cooking class should be booked in advance. Wear comfortable, casual clothing as the kitchen can be warm. Bring an extra bag for market purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to a nearby natural wonder — a national park, rice terraces, cave system, or mountain viewpoint depending on the resort's region. Guided hike or nature walk with a certified eco-guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local ethnic minority village or traditional craft village. Engage with artisans, try your hand at traditional weaving or pottery, and learn about indigenous Vietnamese culture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a relaxing evening. Optional: private yoga session on the beach at sunset followed by a light, healthy dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hearty resort breakfast to fuel the day's adventure — Vietnamese noodle soup, fresh-pressed juices, and tropical fruit platters
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the resort in a scenic natural setting — artisan sandwiches, Vietnamese rice paper rolls, and chilled drinks
meals.dinner: Healthy gourmet dinner at the resort's wellness restaurant — fresh herbs, organic vegetables, and locally sourced proteins with herbal teas

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy hiking shoes and bring insect repellent for the nature excursion. The ethnic village visit should be done respectfully — ask before photographing locals.

day_by_day.morning: Private chartered speedboat or seaplane excursion to a remote island or secluded beach. Enjoy swimming, kayaking, and paddleboarding in pristine waters away from tourist crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Island exploration — snorkeling over coral reefs, beachcombing, or simply relaxing in a private cabana with butler service on the island.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort and enjoy a premium cocktail masterclass at the resort bar — learn to craft classic Vietnamese-inspired cocktails using local spirits, herbs, and tropical fruits.

meals.breakfast: Light resort breakfast before departure — fresh pastries, Vietnamese yogurt with honey, and tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Private BBQ seafood lunch on the island — lobster, tiger prawns, and fresh fish grilled over open coals with local dipping sauces and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's premium restaurant — a chef's tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring the best of Vietnamese coastal cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book the island charter well in advance. Bring waterproof bags for electronics. The cocktail masterclass is typically 1.5 hours and should be reserved through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Cultural deep-dive: visit a local Buddhist pagoda or Cham temple complex for a morning meditation session with monks. Learn about Vietnamese spiritual traditions and architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a vibrant local street food district on foot with a private food anthropologist guide. Discover hidden alleyway eateries, century-old noodle shops, and regional delicacies not found in tourist guides.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a premium cultural event — a classical Vietnamese music performance (nhã nhạc), a traditional dance show, or a lantern festival if seasonally available.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Vietnamese breakfast at a renowned local institution — bún bò Huế or bánh cuốn with fresh herbs and premium Vietnamese drip coffee
meals.lunch: Multi-stop street food lunch guided tour — bún chả, cơm tấm, chè (Vietnamese sweet soup), and regional specialties
meals.dinner: Elegant dinner at a heritage villa restaurant — Vietnamese imperial cuisine inspired by royal court recipes, served in a candlelit garden setting

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) for temple visits. The cultural evening event should be booked in advance as seats are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury bicycle tour through the countryside — ride through rice paddies, lotus ponds, and rural villages at a leisurely pace with a knowledgeable local guide. Stop at a traditional family home for tea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local artisan workshop — silk weaving, traditional lacquerware painting, or hand-embroidery. Participate in a hands-on workshop and commission a bespoke piece as a keepsake.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner at a renowned chef's table experience — a 7-course Vietnamese tasting menu prepared tableside by a celebrated local chef with wine and cocktail pairings.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast featuring Vietnamese-style eggs benedict with pork belly and a fried egg on crispy rice, fresh juices, and smoothies
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch at a countryside restaurant — organic vegetables, free-range chicken, and herbs sourced directly from the surrounding farms
meals.dinner: 7-course chef's table tasting menu at a celebrated fine dining establishment — innovative Vietnamese cuisine with premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The chef's table dinner must be reserved well in advance and may require a deposit. The bicycle tour is best enjoyed in the morning before the midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the resort — sleep in, enjoy a spa treatment, or take a private yoga or tai chi session on the beach. Optional: early morning swim in the resort's infinity pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Curated luxury shopping experience — visit high-end boutiques, silk tailors, and premium Vietnamese fashion designers. Have a bespoke ao dai (traditional Vietnamese dress) or shirt custom-made.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset cruise on a private chartered junk boat or luxury yacht — enjoy canapés, champagne, and panoramic coastal views as the sun sets over the water.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent in-room breakfast service — Vietnamese breakfast spread with pho, fresh fruit, pastries, and premium coffee delivered to your suite
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at a chic beachside restaurant — Mediterranean-Vietnamese fusion cuisine with fresh seafood and craft cocktails
meals.dinner: Dinner on the private yacht or junk boat — a curated seafood feast with champagne and live acoustic Vietnamese music

day_by_day.notes: The bespoke tailor requires at least 2–3 days for alterations, so confirm this was arranged earlier in the trip. The sunset cruise should be booked 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — take one last swim, enjoy the resort's facilities, or take a peaceful walk along the beach to collect memories. Optional: final Vietnamese coffee at a local café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to the airport. Time permitting, stop at a local market for last-minute premium souvenirs — Vietnamese coffee, artisan chocolates, silk scarves, or lacquerware.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through Vietnam's culture, cuisine, and coastal beauty.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — a leisurely spread of both Vietnamese and international favorites, savored without rush
meals.lunch: Quick but quality lunch at a premium airport lounge or a final meal at a beloved local restaurant near the resort before transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at the transit airport lounge

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all custom-made items (ao dai, lacquerware) are packed securely. Keep Vietnamese Dong for any last-minute purchases. Confirm airport transfer timing with the concierge the evening before. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure.
